title: How to get rich (a joke)
takeaway: A joke with a sting: in a corrupt system, honest people struggle.
scene: The heading means 'A humorous rubai', a four-line comic poem. The poet, a doctor himself, sarcastically gives 'advice' on how to get ahead.

original: پانی پانی کر گئی آج دے فرزانے دی گل
زندہ رہن واسطے راہ شرافت دے نہ چل
transliteration: Paani paani kar gayi ajj de farzaane di gall
Zinda rehan vaaste raah sharaafat de na chal
translation: Today's wise man's advice left me red-faced with shame:
'If you want to survive, don't walk the path of decency.'
couplets.story: A 'clever' person gave him some advice so shameless it made him blush: if you want to get by, forget about being honest and decent.

original: ڈاکٹر بن ڈاکو بن افسر یا چپڑاسی بن
جا وکیلاں کولوں سکھ سائل نوں کھاون دے ول
transliteration: Doctor ban, daaku ban, afsar ya chapraasi ban
Ja vakeelaan kolon sikh saail nu khaavan de vall
translation: Become a doctor, a bandit, an officer or an office peon;
go and learn from the lawyers how to eat up your clients.
couplets.story: The joke goes on: become a doctor, a robber, an official or even an office errand-boy, it's all the same. And go learn from lawyers how to squeeze every penny out of the people who come to you for help.

why: It's funny, and it makes a serious point. The poet, himself a doctor, includes doctors in the joke.
prompt: Is it harder to be honest when it seems like dishonest people get ahead? Why stay honest anyway?
